 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,

# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation.

# Operation Specifications
Game::skipPipe
Summary:
Skips the current head pipe by consuming it from the queue and advancing the step count.
Algorithm:
1. Consume the current head pipe from pipeQueue.
2. Increment numOfSteps.
Related Features:
- numOfSteps: step counter incremented when skipping.
- pipeQueue: current pipe is removed from the queue.
Related Classes: PipeQueue
Input:
- None.
Output:
- None.
Pre-condition:
- Game is initialized.
- pipeQueue contains at least one pipe.
Post-condition:
- The current head pipe is removed from the queue.
- numOfSteps is incremented by 1.

Game::undoStep
Summary:
Undoes the last successful pipe placement by restoring the last placed pipe to the front of the queue, clearing the map cell, and incrementing the step count.
Algorithm:
1. If cellStack has no placed cell to undo, return false.
2. Pop the last placed FillableCell from cellStack.
3. Restore the removed cell's pipe to the front of pipeQueue using undo(pipe).
4. Clear the corresponding cell on the map.
5. Increment numOfSteps.
6. Return true.
Related Features:
- numOfSteps: step counter incremented on successful undo.
- cellStack: provides the last placed cell to undo.
- pipeQueue: receives the restored pipe at the front of the queue.
- map: clears the undone placement from the grid.
Related Classes: CellStack, Map, PipeQueue, FillableCell, Pipe
Input:
- None.
Output:
- boolean: true if an undo was performed; false if there were no steps to undo.
Pre-condition:
- Game is initialized.
- If the operation is to succeed, cellStack contains at least one placed cell.
Post-condition:
- On success, the last placed pipe is removed from the map and restored to the front of the queue.
- On success, numOfSteps is incremented by 1.
- On failure, the game state is unchanged.

Game::placePipe
Summary:
Places the current head pipe from the queue at the specified playable cell, using the player-facing column letter mapping.
Algorithm:
1. Convert the input column letter to an internal column index by computing col - 'A' + 1.
2. Keep the row value unchanged.
3. Read the current head pipe from pipeQueue.
4. Attempt to place that pipe into map at cells[row][internalCol] through the map placement logic.
5. If placement succeeds, consume the pipe from the queue, push the placed cell onto cellStack, and increment numOfSteps.
6. Return whether the placement succeeded.
Related Features:
- numOfSteps: step counter incremented on successful placement.
- cellStack: stores the last placed fillable cell for undo.
- pipeQueue: provides the current head pipe to place and is consumed on success.
- map: receives the pipe placement attempt.
Related Classes: CellStack, DelayBar, Map, PipeQueue, Pipe
Input:
- row: the playable row index, aligned with internal Cell[][] indices and expected to be in [1..rows-2].
- col: the player-facing column letter, mapped to internal column index by col - 'A' + 1.
Output:
- boolean: true if the pipe is successfully placed; otherwise false.
Pre-condition:
- Game is initialized.
- pipeQueue is non-empty.
- The mapped target cell exists in the playable area.
Post-condition:
- On success, the current pipe is placed on the map at cells[row][col - 'A' + 1].
- On success, the head pipe is removed from the queue.
- On success, the placed cell is recorded in cellStack.
- On success, numOfSteps is incremented by 1.
- On failure, the game state is unchanged.

Game::hasLost
Summary:
Determines whether the game is currently in a losing state.
Algorithm:
1. Ask the map whether the last water-expansion round filled no new tiles.
2. Return the map's loss result.
3. The game-level loss check is only meaningful after the delay has ended, i.e. when water flow is active.
Related Features:
- map: delegates loss evaluation to the map.
- delayBar: used implicitly to determine whether loss checking is relevant in the current phase.
Related Classes: Map, DelayBar, Game
Input:
- None.
Output:
- boolean: true if the previous water fill round produced zero new filled tiles; otherwise false.
Pre-condition:
- Game is initialized.
- Water-flow phase has started for the current round sequence.
Post-condition:
- No state is modified.

Game::hasWon
Summary:
Determines whether a connected path from source to sink exists.
Algorithm:
1. Delegate path checking to map.checkPath().
2. Return the result.
Related Features:
- map: used for connectivity traversal.
Related Classes: Map, Game
Input:
- None.
Output:
- boolean: true if the source can reach the sink through valid connectivity; otherwise false.
Pre-condition:
- Game is initialized.
Post-condition:
- No state is modified.

Game::updateState
Summary:
Advances the game by one round of state update, typically combining delay countdown and water propagation.
Algorithm:
1. Decrement the delay bar by calling countdown().
2. Read the current propagation distance from delayBar.distance().
3. If the distance is greater than 0, instruct the map to fill water tiles up to that distance.
4. If the distance is not greater than 0, no water expansion occurs yet or the game remains in delay phase.
5. Any loss checking is conceptually deferred until after delay ends.
Related Features:
- delayBar: countdown and propagation timing.
- map: water expansion and loss-state bookkeeping.
Related Classes: DelayBar, Map, Game
Input:
- None.
Output:
- None.
Pre-condition:
- Game is initialized.
Post-condition:
- delayBar.currentValue is reduced by 1.
- If distance > 0, map.fillTiles(distance) has been applied and map fill-tracking state may change.
- Game state reflects the passage of one round.

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation. 
```

# Operation Specifications
Game::skipPipe
Summary:
Skips the current head pipe by consuming it from the queue and advancing the step count.
Algorithm:
1. Consume the current head pipe from pipeQueue.
2. Increment numOfSteps.
Related Features:
- numOfSteps: step counter incremented when skipping.
- pipeQueue: current pipe is removed from the queue.
Related Classes: PipeQueue
Input:
- None.
Output:
- None.
Pre-condition:
- Game is initialized.
- pipeQueue contains at least one pipe.
Post-condition:
- The current head pipe is removed from the queue.
- numOfSteps is incremented by 1.

Game::undoStep
Summary:
Undoes the last successful pipe placement by restoring the last placed pipe to the front of the queue, clearing the map cell, and incrementing the step count.
Algorithm:
1. If cellStack has no placed cell to undo, return false.
2. Pop the last placed FillableCell from cellStack.
3. Restore the removed cell's pipe to the front of pipeQueue using undo(pipe).
4. Clear the corresponding cell on the map.
5. Increment numOfSteps.
6. Return true.
Related Features:
- numOfSteps: step counter incremented on successful undo.
- cellStack: provides the last placed cell to undo.
- pipeQueue: receives the restored pipe at the front of the queue.
- map: clears the undone placement from the grid.
Related Classes: CellStack, Map, PipeQueue, FillableCell, Pipe
Input:
- None.
Output:
- boolean: true if an undo was performed; false if there were no steps to undo.
Pre-condition:
- Game is initialized.
- If the operation is to succeed, cellStack contains at least one placed cell.
Post-condition:
- On success, the last placed pipe is removed from the map and restored to the front of the queue.
- On success, numOfSteps is incremented by 1.
- On failure, the game state is unchanged.

Game::placePipe
Summary:
Places the current head pipe from the queue at the specified playable cell, using the player-facing column letter mapping.
Algorithm:
1. Convert the input column letter to an internal column index by computing col - 'A' + 1.
2. Keep the row value unchanged.
3. Read the current head pipe from pipeQueue.
4. Attempt to place that pipe into map at cells[row][internalCol] through the map placement logic.
5. If placement succeeds, consume the pipe from the queue, push the placed cell onto cellStack, and increment numOfSteps.
6. Return whether the placement succeeded.
Related Features:
- numOfSteps: step counter incremented on successful placement.
- cellStack: stores the last placed fillable cell for undo.
- pipeQueue: provides the current head pipe to place and is consumed on success.
- map: receives the pipe placement attempt.
Related Classes: CellStack, DelayBar, Map, PipeQueue, Pipe
Input:
- row: the playable row index, aligned with internal Cell[][] indices and expected to be in [1..rows-2].
- col: the player-facing column letter, mapped to internal column index by col - 'A' + 1.
Output:
- boolean: true if the pipe is successfully placed; otherwise false.
Pre-condition:
- Game is initialized.
- pipeQueue is non-empty.
- The mapped target cell exists in the playable area.
Post-condition:
- On success, the current pipe is placed on the map at cells[row][col - 'A' + 1].
- On success, the head pipe is removed from the queue.
- On success, the placed cell is recorded in cellStack.
- On success, numOfSteps is incremented by 1.
- On failure, the game state is unchanged.

Game::hasLost
Summary:
Determines whether the game is currently in a losing state.
Algorithm:
1. Ask the map whether the last water-expansion round filled no new tiles.
2. Return the map's loss result.
3. The game-level loss check is only meaningful after the delay has ended, i.e. when water flow is active.
Related Features:
- map: delegates loss evaluation to the map.
- delayBar: used implicitly to determine whether loss checking is relevant in the current phase.
Related Classes: Map, DelayBar, Game
Input:
- None.
Output:
- boolean: true if the previous water fill round produced zero new filled tiles; otherwise false.
Pre-condition:
- Game is initialized.
- Water-flow phase has started for the current round sequence.
Post-condition:
- No state is modified.

Game::hasWon
Summary:
Determines whether a connected path from source to sink exists.
Algorithm:
1. Delegate path checking to map.checkPath().
2. Return the result.
Related Features:
- map: used for connectivity traversal.
Related Classes: Map, Game
Input:
- None.
Output:
- boolean: true if the source can reach the sink through valid connectivity; otherwise false.
Pre-condition:
- Game is initialized.
Post-condition:
- No state is modified.

Game::updateState
Summary:
Advances the game by one round of state update, typically combining delay countdown and water propagation.
Algorithm:
1. Decrement the delay bar by calling countdown().
2. Read the current propagation distance from delayBar.distance().
3. If the distance is greater than 0, instruct the map to fill water tiles up to that distance.
4. If the distance is not greater than 0, no water expansion occurs yet or the game remains in delay phase.
5. Any loss checking is conceptually deferred until after delay ends.
Related Features:
- delayBar: countdown and propagation timing.
- map: water expansion and loss-state bookkeeping.
Related Classes: DelayBar, Map, Game
Input:
- None.
Output:
- None.
Pre-condition:
- Game is initialized.
Post-condition:
- delayBar.currentValue is reduced by 1.
- If distance > 0, map.fillTiles(distance) has been applied and map fill-tracking state may change.
- Game state reflects the passage of one round.

# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation.

# Operation Specifications
Game::skipPipe
Summary:
Skips the current head pipe by consuming it from the queue and advancing the step count.
Algorithm:
1. Consume the current head pipe from pipeQueue.
2. Increment numOfSteps.
Related Features:
- numOfSteps: step counter incremented when skipping.
- pipeQueue: current pipe is removed from the queue.
Related Classes: PipeQueue
Input:
- None.
Output:
- None.
Pre-condition:
- Game is initialized.
- pipeQueue contains at least one pipe.
Post-condition:
- The current head pipe is removed from the queue.
- numOfSteps is incremented by 1.

Game::undoStep
Summary:
Undoes the last successful pipe placement by restoring the last placed pipe to the front of the queue, clearing the map cell, and incrementing the step count.
Algorithm:
1. If cellStack has no placed cell to undo, return false.
2. Pop the last placed FillableCell from cellStack.
3. Restore the removed cell's pipe to the front of pipeQueue using undo(pipe).
4. Clear the corresponding cell on the map.
5. Increment numOfSteps.
6. Return true.
Related Features:
- numOfSteps: step counter incremented on successful undo.
- cellStack: provides the last placed cell to undo.
- pipeQueue: receives the restored pipe at the front of the queue.
- map: clears the undone placement from the grid.
Related Classes: CellStack, Map, PipeQueue, FillableCell, Pipe
Input:
- None.
Output:
- boolean: true if an undo was performed; false if there were no steps to undo.
Pre-condition:
- Game is initialized.
- If the operation is to succeed, cellStack contains at least one placed cell.
Post-condition:
- On success, the last placed pipe is removed from the map and restored to the front of the queue.
- On success, numOfSteps is incremented by 1.
- On failure, the game state is unchanged.

Game::placePipe
Summary:
Places the current head pipe from the queue at the specified playable cell, using the player-facing column letter mapping.
Algorithm:
1. Convert the input column letter to an internal column index by computing col - 'A' + 1.
2. Keep the row value unchanged.
3. Read the current head pipe from pipeQueue.
4. Attempt to place that pipe into map at the target cell through the map placement logic.
5. If placement succeeds, consume the pipe from the queue, push the placed cell onto cellStack, and increment numOfSteps.
6. Return whether the placement succeeded.
Related Features:
- numOfSteps: step counter incremented on successful placement.
- cellStack: stores the last placed fillable cell for undo.
- pipeQueue: provides the current head pipe to place and is consumed on success.
- map: receives the pipe placement attempt.
Related Classes: CellStack, Map, PipeQueue, Pipe
Input:
- row: the playable row index, aligned with internal Cell[][] indices and expected to be in [1..rows-2].
- col: the player-facing column letter, mapped to internal column index by col - 'A' + 1.
Output:
- boolean: true if the pipe is successfully placed; otherwise false.
Pre-condition:
- Game is initialized.
- pipeQueue is non-empty.
- The mapped target cell exists in the playable area.
Post-condition:
- On success, the current pipe is placed on the map at cells[row][col - 'A' + 1].
- On success, the head pipe is removed from the queue.
- On success, the placed cell is recorded in cellStack.
- On success, numOfSteps is incremented by 1.
- On failure, the game state is unchanged.

Game::hasLost
Summary:
Determines whether the game is currently in a losing state.
Algorithm:
1. Return the game's loss result from map.hasLost().
2. The loss condition becomes meaningful only after the delay has ended, i.e. when water flow is active.
Related Features:
- map: delegates loss evaluation to the map.
- delayBar: used to indicate whether loss checking is relevant in the current phase.
Related Classes: Map, DelayBar
Input:
- None.
Output:
- boolean: true if the previous water fill round produced zero new filled tiles; otherwise false.
Pre-condition:
- Game is initialized.
- Water-flow phase has started for the current round sequence.
Post-condition:
- No state is modified.

Game::hasWon
Summary:
Determines whether a connected path from source to sink exists.
Algorithm:
1. Delegate path checking to map.checkPath().
2. Return the result.
Related Features:
- map: used for connectivity traversal.
Related Classes: Map
Input:
- None.
Output:
- boolean: true if the source can reach the sink through valid connectivity; otherwise false.
Pre-condition:
- Game is initialized.
Post-condition:
- No state is modified.

Game::updateState
Summary:
Advances the game by one round of state update, typically combining delay countdown and water propagation.
Algorithm:
1. Decrement the delay bar by calling countdown().
2. Read the current propagation distance from delayBar.distance().
3. If the distance is greater than 0, instruct the map to fill water tiles up to that distance.
4. If the distance is not greater than 0, no water expansion occurs yet or the game remains in delay phase.
5. Any loss checking is conceptually deferred until after delay ends.
Related Features:
- delayBar: countdown and propagation timing.
- map: water expansion and loss-state bookkeeping.
Related Classes: DelayBar, Map
Input:
- None.
Output:
- None.
Pre-condition:
- Game is initialized.
Post-condition:
- delayBar.currentValue is reduced by 1.
- If distance > 0, map.fillTiles(distance) has been applied and map fill-tracking state may change.
- Game state reflects the passage of one round.

# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation. 
```

# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation. 
```

# Operation Specifications
DelayBar::distance
Summary:
Returns the water-flow distance represented by the current delay state.
Algorithm:
1. Compute the negation of currentValue.
2. Return the result.
Related Features:
- currentValue: used to derive the returned distance.
Related Classes: DelayBar
Input:
- None.
Output:
- int: the negated currentValue.
- During countdown, the result is negative.
- After countdown reaches zero, the result is zero.
- After delay ends and countdown continues past zero, the result is positive, representing propagation distance.
Pre-condition:
- DelayBar is initialized.
Post-condition:
- No state is modified.

DelayBar::countdown
Summary:
Decrements the delay timer by one round.
Algorithm:
1. Subtract 1 from currentValue.
2. Keep initialValue unchanged.
Related Features:
- currentValue: countdown state.
- initialValue: unchanged reference starting delay.
Related Classes: DelayBar
Input:
- None.
Output:
- None.
Pre-condition:
- DelayBar is initialized.
Post-condition:
- currentValue is reduced by 1.
- The timer may become zero or negative after repeated calls, indicating delay expiration and water-flow phase.

# Operation Specifications
DelayBar::distance
Summary:
Returns the water-flow distance represented by the current delay state.
Algorithm:
1. Compute the negation of currentValue.
2. Return the result.
Related Features:
- currentValue: used to derive the returned distance.
Related Classes: DelayBar
Input:
- None.
Output:
- int: the negated currentValue.
- During countdown, the result is negative.
- After countdown reaches zero, the result is zero.
- After delay ends and countdown continues past zero, the result is positive, representing propagation distance.
Pre-condition:
- DelayBar is initialized.
Post-condition:
- No state is modified.

DelayBar::countdown
Summary:
Decrements the delay timer by one round.
Algorithm:
1. Subtract 1 from currentValue.
2. Keep initialValue unchanged.
Related Features:
- currentValue: countdown state.
- initialValue: unchanged reference starting delay.
Related Classes: DelayBar
Input:
- None.
Output:
- None.
Pre-condition:
- DelayBar is initialized.
Post-condition:
- currentValue is reduced by 1.
- The timer may become zero or negative after repeated calls, indicating delay expiration and water-flow phase.

# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation. 
```

# Operation Specifications
Map::tryPlacePipe
Summary:
Attempts to place a pipe into a playable cell using internal array indices directly, without any coordinate conversion.
Algorithm:
1. Verify that row and col are within the playable range [1..rows-2] and [1..cols-2].
2. Verify that the target cell at cell[row][col] is a FillableCell.
3. Verify that the target cell is not already occupied by a pipe.
4. If all checks pass, store the given pipe in the target FillableCell and return true.
5. Otherwise, return false.
Related Features:
- cell: 2D grid storing the map cells.
- rows: row dimension of the map.
- cols: column dimension of the map.
Related Classes: Pipe, FillableCell, Cell
Input:
- row: internal row index, expected to be in [1..rows-2].
- col: internal column index, expected to be in [1..cols-2].
- pipe: the pipe to place.
Output:
- boolean: true if the pipe is successfully placed; otherwise false.
Pre-condition:
- Map is initialized.
- pipe is not null.
Post-condition:
- On success, the specified FillableCell contains the given pipe.
- On failure, the map remains unchanged.

Map::fillTiles
Summary:
Expands water from the source through connected pipes up to the specified distance using breadth-first-style traversal.
Algorithm:
1. If distance is less than or equal to the previously processed fill distance, do nothing.
2. Otherwise start from the source cell and/or the frontier recorded in filledTiles.
3. For each reachable pipe cell, inspect neighboring cells in all connection directions.
4. A neighbor is eligible only if:
   - it is a pipe cell,
   - it has a matching connection back to the current cell, i.e. opposite directions are compatible.
5. Mark newly reached pipe cells as filled.
6. Record newly filled coordinates in filledTiles.
7. Update prevFilledDistance and prevFilledTiles to reflect the newly processed round.
Related Features:
- filledTiles: records coordinates filled by water.
- prevFilledDistance: prevents reprocessing of the same distance.
- prevFilledTiles: used for loss detection.
- sourceCell: starting point for propagation.
- cell: 2D map storage for cell lookup.
Related Classes: Map, Coordinate, TerminationCell, FillableCell, Pipe, Direction
Input:
- distance: propagation depth measured from the source; expected to be non-negative and increasing over time.
Output:
- None.
Pre-condition:
- Map is initialized.
- sourceCell exists.
- distance is a valid non-negative progression step.
Post-condition:
- All reachable pipes within the specified distance are marked filled.
- filledTiles contains the coordinates of tiles newly filled in this update sequence.
- prevFilledDistance and prevFilledTiles are updated consistently for later win/loss checks.

Map::undo
Summary:
Clears a previously placed pipe from the specified map cell.
Algorithm:
1. Locate the cell at the provided coordinate.
2. Verify the cell is a FillableCell.
3. Remove its stored pipe, if any.
4. Do not alter border walls, termination cells, or unrelated cells.
Related Features:
- cell: underlying map storage.
Related Classes: Map, Coordinate, FillableCell
Input:
- coord: coordinate of the cell to restore; uses internal row/col array indices directly.
Output:
- None.
Pre-condition:
- Map is initialized.
- coord refers to a valid cell location.
Post-condition:
- If the target cell is fillable, its pipe is cleared.
- The cell becomes empty again, ready for future placement.

Map::hasLost
Summary:
Determines whether the current water-expansion round produced no newly filled tiles.
Algorithm:
1. Compare prevFilledTiles with zero.
2. Return true if prevFilledTiles == 0; otherwise return false.
Related Features:
- prevFilledTiles: tracks the number of tiles filled in the previous round.
Related Classes: Map
Input:
- None.
Output:
- boolean: true when no new pipes were filled in the previous round; otherwise false.
Pre-condition:
- Map is initialized.
- fillTiles has been executed at least for the relevant round sequence.
Post-condition:
- No state is modified.

  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation. 
```

# Operation Specifications
Map::tryPlacePipe
Summary:
Attempts to place a pipe into a playable cell using internal array indices directly, without any coordinate conversion.
Algorithm:
1. Verify that row and col are within the playable range [1..rows-2] and [1..cols-2].
2. Verify that the target cell at cell[row][col] is a FillableCell.
3. Verify that the target cell is not already occupied by a pipe.
4. If all checks pass, store the given pipe in the target FillableCell and return true.
5. Otherwise, return false.
Related Features:
- cell: 2D grid storing the map cells.
- rows: row dimension of the map.
- cols: column dimension of the map.
Related Classes: Pipe, FillableCell, Cell
Input:
- row: internal row index, expected to be in [1..rows-2].
- col: internal column index, expected to be in [1..cols-2].
- pipe: the pipe to place.
Output:
- boolean: true if the pipe is successfully placed; otherwise false.
Pre-condition:
- Map is initialized.
- pipe is not null.
Post-condition:
- On success, the specified FillableCell contains the given pipe.
- On failure, the map remains unchanged.

Map::fillTiles
Summary:
Expands water from the source through connected pipes up to the specified distance using breadth-first-style traversal.
Algorithm:
1. If distance is less than or equal to the previously processed fill distance, do nothing.
2. Otherwise start from the source cell and/or the frontier recorded in filledTiles.
3. For each reachable pipe cell, inspect neighboring cells in all connection directions.
4. A neighbor is eligible only if:
   - it is a pipe cell,
   - it has a matching connection back to the current cell, i.e. opposite directions are compatible.
5. Mark newly reached pipe cells as filled.
6. Record newly filled coordinates in filledTiles.
7. Update prevFilledDistance and prevFilledTiles to reflect the newly processed round.
Related Features:
- filledTiles: records coordinates filled by water.
- prevFilledDistance: prevents reprocessing of the same distance.
- prevFilledTiles: used for loss detection.
- sourceCell: starting point for propagation.
- cell: 2D map storage for cell lookup.
Related Classes: Map, Coordinate, TerminationCell, FillableCell, Pipe, Direction
Input:
- distance: propagation depth measured from the source; expected to be non-negative and increasing over time.
Output:
- None.
Pre-condition:
- Map is initialized.
- sourceCell exists.
- distance is a valid non-negative progression step.
Post-condition:
- All reachable pipes within the specified distance are marked filled.
- filledTiles contains the coordinates of tiles newly filled in this update sequence.
- prevFilledDistance and prevFilledTiles are updated consistently for later win/loss checks.

Map::undo
Summary:
Clears a previously placed pipe from the specified map cell.
Algorithm:
1. Locate the cell at the provided coordinate.
2. Verify the cell is a FillableCell.
3. Remove its stored pipe, if any.
4. Do not alter border walls, termination cells, or unrelated cells.
Related Features:
- cell: underlying map storage.
Related Classes: Map, Coordinate, FillableCell
Input:
- coord: coordinate of the cell to restore; uses internal row/col array indices directly.
Output:
- None.
Pre-condition:
- Map is initialized.
- coord refers to a valid cell location.
Post-condition:
- If the target cell is fillable, its pipe is cleared.
- The cell becomes empty again, ready for future placement.

Map::hasLost
Summary:
Determines whether the current water-expansion round produced no newly filled tiles.
Algorithm:
1. Compare prevFilledTiles with zero.
2. Return true if prevFilledTiles == 0; otherwise return false.
Related Features:
- prevFilledTiles: tracks the number of tiles filled in the previous round.
Related Classes: Map
Input:
- None.
Output:
- boolean: true when no new pipes were filled in the previous round; otherwise false.
Pre-condition:
- Map is initialized.
- fillTiles has been executed at least for the relevant round sequence.
Post-condition:
- No state is modified.

# Requirement
```text
 Overall/Domain description.
 Console pipe-connection game: grid with outer walls, one source inside pointing inward, one sink on the border
  pointing outward. Player places pipes from a queue; after a delay, water flows along placed pipes.
Cell[][] uses 0-based array indices, but index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are occupied by the outer wall border. Therefore, the playable area starts at internal index 1: [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]. Player-facing coordinates are deliberately aligned with these playable indices: row 1 maps to internal row 1, column 'A' maps to internal col 1. No row-1/col-1 conversion is performed.
 Direction provides four directions plus opposite/offset; PipeShape defines
  connection
  directions; TerminationType distinguishes SOURCE vs SINK.

  Functional Requirements

Coordinate and Direction: Coordinate.row and Coordinate.col represent internal Cell[][] array indices and are used directly as cells[row][col]. A Cell stored at cells[r][c] should have Coordinate(row=r, col=c). 
Because the outer wall border occupies index 0, playable cells naturally start at index 1, so player input aligns with internal playable indices.
  Direction enum provides four directions (UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT) and Pa19Helper provides getOpposite() returning the opposite direction
  and getOffset() returning the unit coordinate offset for movement calculations.

  Game: Operations to place a pipe, skip, undo, advance water flow, check win, check loss; convenience fromString
  constructor; maintain step count. 
Operation placePipe: This method maps the player column letter to an internal column index using col - 'A' + 1, 
keeps row unchanged, and places the pipe at cells[row][colIndex]. For example, placePipe(1, 'A') targets cells[1][1].
Operation skipPipe: Consumes the current pipe from the queue and increments the step count. Operation
  undoStep: Pops the last placed cell from CellStack, restores the pipe to the queue head, clears the cell on the map,
  and increments the step count. Returns false if there are no steps to undo.

  Map: Cells are stored as a 2D array Cell[][] with indices [0..rows-1] × [0..cols-1],
  where index 0 and rows-1/cols-1 are walls (border). The playable area occupies
  internal indices [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], which aligns with 1-based
  user input mapping. tryPlacePipe(row, col, pipe) accepts playable-area aligned coordinates (row and col in [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2]) and uses them
  directly as array indices (no conversion needed due to the wall alignment).
  It rejects: (1) row/col outside [1..rows-2] × [1..cols-2], (2) non-FillableCell,
  or (3) already-occupied cell.

  Cell family: Cell.fromChar parses map chars to concrete cells; FillableCell holds an optional pipe and renders pipe or
  '.'; TerminationCell holds pointingTo direction and Type (SOURCE/SINK), with filled state for rendering; Wall renders
  wall char.

  TerminationCell.toSingleChar: Returns the corresponding arrow character based on the current termination cell's
  filling state and pointingTo direction: when filled, returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Filled; when unfilled,
  returns the arrow from PipePatterns.Unfilled. Both SOURCE and SINK use pointingTo directly without direction reversal.
  Throws IllegalStateException("Invalid pointingTo value!") for unknown direction.

  Pipe: Expose connection directions via getConnections() returning Direction[] based on Shape; char rendering by
  filled/unfilled state; construct from short string code (HZ, VT, TL, TR, BL, BR, CR). getConnections(): Returns the
  list of connection directions based on the current pipe shape; throws IllegalStateException("Unknown shape") if the
  shape is not recognized. toSingleChar(): Returns the character representation of this pipe, different for filled and
  unfilled pipes.

  Water Flow: fillBeginTile() marks the source cell as filled. fillTiles(distance) fills pipes within the specified
  distance from source using BFS-style expansion. Water propagates along pipes only when adjacent pipes have matching
  connection directions (one pipe's direction must be the opposite of the other). Each round increments the fill
  distance by 1.

  Win/Loss Conditions: checkPath() uses BFS to determine if a connected path exists from SOURCE to SINK by following
  (i) from SOURCE, step once in the SOURCE pointingTo direction, and (ii) from a pipe cell, step in each pipe connection direction.
  It does not require the traversed pipes to be filled; reaching the SINK cell implies win. hasLost() returns true when prevFilledTiles == 0,
  meaning no new pipes were filled in the previous round (loss condition). The game checks loss only after delay has ended (distance > 0).

  PipeQueue: peek/consume/undo head pipe and auto-refill to fixed length with random shapes. undo(Pipe) inserts the pipe
  back to the front of the queue.

  DelayBar: countdown() decrements the current value by 1 each round. distance() returns -currentValue, representing how
  far the water should flow (negative during countdown, positive after delay ends).

  CellStack: push/pop last placement; undoCount counts the number of successful undo actions (i.e., successful pop
  operations), not the current stack size; 

  External/Tool Classes (not generated; handwritten or reused,You only need to assume that these Java files mentioned below are already in the pa19 package.)
  Pa19Helper is a small helper/assembly class used to build core game model objects for this project. It provides
  convenience methods to (1) construct a Game by wiring together Map, PipeQueue, DelayBar, and CellStack from given
  inputs, and (2) create/parse basic elements (e.g., Map from a Cell[][] or string representation, map characters/short
  codes into Cell/Pipe). It also centralizes simple direction utilities (opposite direction and unit offsets) used
  during parsing and movement-related calculations.
  Deserializer: Purpose: deserialize map input into runtime objects. Field: Path path (input file path). Constructors:
  Deserializer(String path) delegates to private Deserializer(Path); private Deserializer(Path) validates file existence
  and throws FileNotFoundException if missing. Methods: Game parseGame() reads rows, cols, delay, map lines, and
  optional default pipes, then returns Pa19Helper.createGame(...); on unexpected EOF or I/O failure, returns null
  (and logs error). static Cell[][] parseString(int rows, int cols, String cellsRep) converts multiline text to a Cell
  matrix by character, using Pa19Helper.cellFromChar with SINK type on border cells and SOURCE type on inner
  cells. private String getFirstNonEmptyLine(BufferedReader br) returns the first non-blank, non-comment line (ignores
  lines starting with #), or null at end of stream.

  PipePatterns: Purpose: central constant repository for all map-rendering characters. Design: final utility class with
  private constructor (non-instantiable). Exposed constants: WALL (solid wall block), plus two nested static groups:
  Filled and Unfilled. Each group defines arrow chars (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, LEFT_ARROW, RIGHT_ARROW) and pipe-shape
  chars (HORIZONTAL, VERTICAL, TOP_LEFT, TOP_RIGHT, BOTTOM_LEFT, BOTTOM_RIGHT, CROSS). Use PipePatterns constants for
  all rendering chars; do not hardcode glyphs in TerminationCell and PipeShape logic.

  StringUtils: Purpose: provide lightweight string helper utilities. Class design: utility class with a private
  constructor to prevent instantiation. 
```
